title: Culture of Primary Human Tracheobronchial Epithelial Cells
protocol: If not already prepared, make BEGM by thawing growth supplements and adding to the basal medium and sterile filter (0.22 um pore).
Add 18 mL of growth medium to the flask and pre-equilibrate in the incubator for approximately 30 minutes.
Place vial(s) in a 37 °C water bath; swirl frequently to check if contents have thawed, usually takes less than three minutes.
Spray the vial with 70% ethanol to reduce surface contaminants.
Pipette the vial contents up and down to resuspend the cells; add cells to the pre-equilibrated T75 flask.
Alternatively, add the cells to a tube of pre-equilibrated medium, centrifuge at 1000 RPM for five minutes, then resuspend pellet in fresh medium and add to the flask.
Place flasks in a CO₂ incubator (5% CO₂, 37 °C).
Check cultures under the microscope to determine if cells have attached to the plastic.
Aspirate the media and replace with 15 mL of fresh BEGM.
Place flasks back into the incubator.
Aspirate media and replace with 18 mL of BEGM.
Replace media every two days.
When cells reach approximately 80-100% confluence, passage cells into more T75 flasks.
Aspirate off media.
Add 4 mL of trypsin-EDTA solution to each T75 flask and incubate at 37°C for 2-3 minutes.
When approximately 80-90% of the cells are detached, add a half volume of SBTI to the flask.
Pipette up the trypsin/SBTI mixture and rinse the flask bottom.
Mix trypsin and SBTI to aid in their combination.
Transfer the cells to a sterile centrifuge tube. Cells from individual flasks can be combined.
Centrifuge the cells at 1000 RPM for five minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate off the supernatant. Tap the pellet to break it up. Add 10 mL BEGM and vigorously pipet to create a homogeneous suspension.
Transfer a 10 μL aliquot of the cell suspension to a hemocytometer and count the cells.
Add 5 x 10^5 cells/T75 flask. The final volume of BEGM should be 18ml/flask.
Culture cells as above, changing the media every two days until cells reach confluence.
When flasks reach confluence: cryopreserve the cells.
Transfer the confluent cells to Transwells or other plastic ware for studies.
Further passage the cells.
Adjust cell density to the desired level by adding more media or centrifuging and re-suspending in less media.
Neutralize trypsin with SBTI after cells have been removed.
Count the cells after neutralizing trypsin.
Determine the number of inserts to be seeded for Transwells.
Calculate the total volume needed based on the number of inserts and seeding density.
Calculate the total number of cells required for all inserts plus a fudge factor.
Resuspend cells at a concentration of 1 million/ml if necessary.
Add 4.2 mL of cell suspension to 6.3 mL of additional medium to achieve the desired plating density.
Let cells adhere for 16-24 hours in Transwells.
Aspirate off nonadherent cells after the adhesion period.
Add fresh medium apically after aspirating nonadherent cells.
Feed cells basolaterally every other 48 hours once confluence is reached.
Trypsinize the cells as usual.
Determine the number of cells present and repellet.
Resuspend the pellet in Cell Freezing Medium (10^6 cells/1.5-2.0 mL) and pipet up and down to mix.
Transfer to cryovials and let sit on ice for 20 minutes.
Place cooler in a -80 °C freezer for 16-24 hours.
Place vial in liquid N₂.
Observe cells microscopically to ensure there is no bacterial or fungal contamination.
Do not use cells that fail to reach confluence for further passaging or experimental procedures.
Consider carefully before proceeding if cells show unusual morphology.
Check CO₂ concentration periodically (at least once per week) using a Fyrite test kit.
Monitor temperature within the chambers with a thermometer.
Clean incubators periodically (at least every two weeks) with antibacterial/antifungal agents.
Add an antifungal agent (benzalkonium chloride) to internal water trays to deter growth of contaminants.
